senses.gloss:
Gotama
------------------------------------------
Gotama is a sage mentioned in the Ṛgveda several times, (vide 1.62.13; 1.78.2; 4.4.11) but not as the seer (draṣṭā) of mantras. He was closely connected with the Aṅgirasas (descendant of अङ्गिरस्). His patronymic was Rāhūgaṇa (descendant of Rahūgaṇa). The Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (1.4.1.10) says he was the पुरोहित (family priest) of Māthva Videgha and a bearer of Vedic civilisation. His name also finds a place in the Atharvaveda (4.29.6). Vāma-deva and Nodhas were his sons.
He is considered as one of the original sages who started the गोत्र tradition.

gotra
(‘that which protects the cows’, ‘a cow-shed’)
------------------------------------------
The words ‘gotra’ and ‘pravara’ have been extensively used in the dharmaśāstra literature, especially while a person has to introduce himself to another and also in connection with marriages.
In its etymological sense, which perhaps indicates its earliest sense, ‘gotra’ means a cowshed (or a cowherd) where the cows of a group of people (most probably relatives) were kept together and protected. But, in course of time, the word acquired the meaning, ‘a common patriarchal ancestor from whom one has descended’.
Gotra was of great importance in several fundamental matters of family affairs like इन्हेरितन्चे or मर्रिअगे and religious ceremonies like śrāddha.
The original sages from whom the gotras are traced, are eight in number: विश्वामित्र, जमदग्नि, भरद्वाज, गौतम, अत्रि, वसिष्ठ, कश्यप and अगस्त्य. In course of time, the number of gotras increased enormously.
When a person mentions his गोत्र by giving the name of one of these sages, it means that he traces his lineage from the ancient sage by unbroken male descent.
Another word which is closely connected with गोत्र is ‘pravara.’ Literally, it means ‘prārthanā’, ‘choosing or invoking’. A synonym for the same is ‘ārṣeya’. So, प्रवर actually means the illustrious sages, ancestors of the yajamāna who is now performing a Vedic sacrifice, who themselves had invoked अग्नि, the deity of fire, in the earlier days, even as he is doing now.
Though the gotras can be almost unlimited, the pravaras have been fixed at 49. The more important gotras (seven only) have been classified into seven gaṇas or groups, the number of sages in each group varying from 3 to 10, and the total 49. These gaṇas are subdivided into pakṣas and the pakṣas, again into gotras.
So, if गोत्र represents the original ancestor from whom the family tree was born and evolved, प्रवर stands for the more important of the ancient ancestors who had performed वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्. The sages of the प्रवर may be more ancient than the sage of गोत्र. Generally these sages (of a प्रवर) mentioned while performing religious rites, are only three.
When a person does not know his गोत्र, he can adopt that of his priest or गुरु (teacher). If even that is not properly known, he can then take Kāśyapa-गोत्र, कश्यप being the original प्रजापति from whom च्रेअतिओन् of living beings started.
When a boy is adopted by a childless couple, he will retain the गोत्र of his original ड़थेर् and also get the one of the foster ड़थेर्.
Marriage between persons of the same गोत्र is prohibited.
